item.title: Tech with Mak Atomic orbitals, photorealistic 3D rendering, and neural networks
item.description:
Tech with Mak
Atomic orbitals, photorealistic 3D rendering, and neural networks share an unexpected piece of mathematics.

3D Gaussian Splatting and quantum mechanics use the same mathematical functions.

They're called Spherical Harmonics, and they connect two seemingly unrelated problems: describing the angular structure of atomic orbitals and representing how a 3D scene looks from different directions.

The mathematics is closely related to Fourier analysis.

Just as sine and cosine functions can be combined to represent periodic signals, spherical harmonics form a mathematical basis for representing functions defined on the surface of a sphere.

Instead of describing how a signal varies over time, they describe how a quantity varies with direction.

This becomes particularly useful in modern AI.

In 3D Gaussian Splatting, each Gaussian can store learned spherical-harmonic coefficients that determine how its color changes with the viewing direction. The original implementation uses harmonics up to degree 3, giving 16 basis functions per color channel.

This allows the renderer to represent view-dependent appearance without assigning a separate color for every possible camera angle.

The same mathematics also appears in geometric deep learning.

Rotation-equivariant neural networks use spherical harmonics to encode spatial directions in a way that transforms predictably when an object is rotated. This is particularly useful in molecular machine learning, where the relative positions and orientations of atoms matter.

And the connection to physics goes even deeper.

In quantum mechanics, spherical harmonics describe the angular part of atomic wavefunctions, helping explain the directional patterns associated with atomic orbitals.

The underlying applications are remarkably different, but the mathematical problem is closely related.

Whether we're describing an electron's angular wavefunction, representing view-dependent color, or learning from 3D molecular geometry, spherical harmonics provide a systematic way to represent information that depends on direction.
tweet

item.title: Puru Saxena AI fears (Dem sweep), Jensen saga, Iran war, Fed hikes not enough...
item.description:
Puru Saxena
AI fears (Dem sweep), Jensen saga, Iran war, Fed hikes not enough....lets increase the tariffs!

TRUMP ADMINISTRATION PROPOSES NEW TARIFFS ON 14 MAJOR TRADING PARTNERS

The U.S. has concluded investigations into structural industrial overcapacity, determining that new trade measures are warranted against 14 major trading partners.

A senior U.S. official outlined proposed tariffs:

🔸 China: 20%, potentially rising to 40% without trade agreements.
🔸 Vietnam: Could face tariffs of 35%.
🔸 EU, Japan, South Korea, India and others: Targeted tariffs under consideration.

Mexico and Norway are excluded from the current proposals.

Officials say the measures will respect existing trade agreements, with tariffs unlikely to take effect before January 2027, following a public notice process.

China faces the highest proposed tariff rate, raising the prospect of renewed trade tensions. - *Walter Bloomberg
tweet

item.description:
Colin Wu
下楼看见保洁大妈在边做卫生边刷短剧，突然有个思考，短剧本身并不是好的商业模式。

首先是观看时长很久，但受众的年龄大、消费水平非常低；第二也是更重要的，短剧很难形成长期 IP，缺乏长尾消费价值。

比如黑悟空，成功了以后可以吃这个 IP 50 年甚至 100 年；而短剧几乎没有让人记住的 IP，看完了爽完了结束了。
tweet
